title.narrative: Operational support programme to strengthen the Ecuadorian response to its security crisis and create resilient communities

description.narrative: cuador has unfortunately become known as the most violent country in Latin America, with a staggering rise in homicides. This has been accompanied by the country's emergence as a major centre for drug trafficking, with organised crime gaining complete control in some coastal regions. The absence of state presence has allowed this dire situation to catch Ecuador off guard, overwhelming law enforcement and administration. Even the nation's exporting sector is now concerned about potential risks to its successful Free Trade Agreement with the EU. The proposed Intervention builds on the previous EU engagement in the security field and suggests complementary issues in two key areas: Shock absorption and reform capacity. Pillar 1: Resilient national institutions towards the drug traffickers and related organized crime activities Strengthening the country's capacity in anti-money laundering and the good governance of the penitentiary system The intervention aims at fostering a structural and systemic change by strengthening the institutional capacity of the specialised investigative units of the Executive, based on the ¿follow the money¿ principle, complementing the efforts of justice & security institutions. Supporting the restructuration of the penitentiary system. The EU is the only international donor currently providing TA in the penitentiary sector. The government will perform extensive structural reforms of the executive's institutions, and the EU can accompany this process by sharing the best practices in line with its democratic and human rights values and rule of law and good governance principles, as stated in the EU SSR Framework to create a sustainable solution vis-à-vis the challenges.  Adaptation and Stabilisation capacities  Pillar 2: Resilient communities & non-governmental actors towards the drug traffickers Improve the private sector's capacity to secure its trading system -. The contamination of containers with drugs from TOCs puts the FTA´s successful implementation at risk. Capacity building and technical assistance to the private sector will positively impact Ecuador´s economic resilience by strengthening its adaptation capacity to come up with constructive solutions. <span style="color
